prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a corridor-like layout: in frames 1–2 a nearby left wall and doorway are bright, roughly 0.5–2 m away, while the darker central and right regions extend several metres into the hall; frame 3 is largely indeterminate. In frame 4, the corridor recedes ahead and a person near the lower centre appears roughly 3–5 m in front of the camera, with the far wall and openings behind them. By frame 5, the right wall becomes very near, about 0.5–1.5 m, while the corridor remains farther ahead; the RGB also shows a person partly cut off at the right edge, but their depth is not cleanly separated. The map makes near-wall versus deep-corridor structure clearer than the dark RGB, but its smooth gradients, missing detail, and brightness changes at frame boundaries make metric distances, occlusion boundaries, and motion estimates unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies no objects in frames 1–3, one person near the lower centre of frame 4, and a person plus a wall clock at the far right of frame 5. The frame-4 person is several metres ahead in the corridor, while the frame-5 person is much nearer—approximately 0.5–1.5 m away—and partly outside the right image boundary; the clock is above that person on the right wall, probably about 1–2 m from them spatially. Across the last two frames, the detected person shifts from distant and near-centre to close and far-right, consistent with camera approach and/or turning right, but the masks do not reveal facing direction or gaze. The map isolates small or partially cropped instances that are difficult to distinguish in the RGB, yet it misses doors, walls, furniture, and any body parts obscured or outside the view, so it is unreliable as a complete inventory.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is empty in all five frames, so it supplies no body or hand keypoints, facing direction, gaze estimate, limb position, or reach information. Using the RGB only for context, the frame-4 person is ahead at roughly 3–5 m and outside the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, while the frame-5 person is close at the right edge—roughly 0.5–1.5 m—and may be near reach, although much of their body is cropped. No reliable statement can be made about whether either person faces or looks toward the camera wearer, or what lies within that person’s own reach. The blank output adds nothing spatially beyond the RGB and is especially unreliable here because the visible people are small, blurred, dark, or partly out of frame.
